s1.syndrome_frame: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal
salient_findings: Nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
key_facts: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness
Initially treated with oral steroids
No hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
Nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal
Mild sensorineural hearing loss at 4000 Hz
Irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen on MRI
Expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve on CT
Erosion of the posterior external auditory canal on CT
Expansion of the stylomastoid foramen on CT
Lesion had heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast on MRI

shortlist.label: Facial nerve schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Gradual-onset unilateral facial weakness with a mass in the ear canal and imaging findings of a lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a cartilaginous mass and microscopic findings of pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei in a myxochondroid matrix

shortlist.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Microscopic findings of pleomorphic cells and a myxochondroid matrix, although less likely given the location and clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a nonpulsatile mass in the ear canal and imaging findings of a lesion with heterogeneous enhancement

shortlist.label: Geniculate ganglion hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the lesion near the stylomastoid foramen and geniculate ganglion, although less common than other diagnoses

raw.rationale: The patient's 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness, nonpulsatile mass in the inferior ear canal, and imaging findings of an irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen with heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast are consistent with a facial nerve schwannoma. The expansion of the fallopian canal and stylomastoid foramen also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: The presence of a cartilaginous specimen is not specific to chondrosarcoma and the imaging findings do not strongly support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Pleomorphic adenoma
rejected.why: This tumor type is more commonly associated with the salivary glands and the imaging findings do not support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Facial nerve hemangioma
rejected.why: The imaging findings do not show the characteristic features of a hemangioma, such as a highly vascular mass

rejected.label: Geniculate ganglion hemangioma
rejected.why: The location of the lesion is not consistent with a geniculate ganglion hemangioma, which typically occurs in the geniculate ganglion
